scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a configuration change on router8, router7 reports that its
OSPF adjacency with router8 dropped (neighbor went INIT/DOWN, then
gone) and some Campus 2 routes flapped. Campus-1-to-Campus-1
traffic still works and Campus 2 PCs reach their local SVI. Find
what broke the router7<->router8 adjacency.

injection.action: change OSPF area for the 172.25.1.0 network to a
injection.command:
vtysh -c "configure terminal" \
        -c "router ospf" \
        -c "no network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0" \
        -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7" \
        -c "exit" -c "exit"
  vtysh -c "clear ip ospf process"

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router8 OSPF area configuration on the
  172.25.1.0/24 link
Mechanism: OSPF requires both ends of an adjacency to agree
  on the area ID. router7's eth5 is 172.25.1.1 in area 0;
  router8's eth4 was 172.25.1.2 in area 0 and was just changed
  to area 7. The hellos now carry mismatched area IDs, so the
  router7<->router8 adjacency drops (Full -> Init -> gone).
  router8 remains in OSPF via its OTHER area-0 links, so traffic
  reroutes and Campus 1 stays mostly reachable -- the observable,
  diagnosable fault is the dropped adjacency on the 172.25.1.0/24
  link, not a full Campus-2 outage.
Localization: router8
Root cause: OSPF area mismatch on the router7<->router8 link
  (router8 in area 7, router7 in area 0)
Fix: on router8 — `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no network
  172.25.1.0/24 area 7" -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0"`
scenario.fix_spec:
on router8 — `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no network
  172.25.1.0/24 area 7" -c "network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0"`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch

agent.diagnosis_text:
The broken component is OSPF on the inter-router link between router7 and router8 (FRR ospfd). The symptom (neighbor seen INIT/DOWN on router7, then gone) matches an area mismatch: OSPF hellos are received but discarded because the peers believe the shared subnet belongs to different areas, so the adjacency never progresses to 2-Way/Full and routes flap as LSAs for that path appear/disappear.

Localization and evidence:
- The physical link is up on both ends with matching IPs: router7 eth5=172.25.1.1/24 and router8 eth4=172.25.1.2/24 (interfaces UP).
- Router7 OSPF config advertises this network in the backbone: “network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0” (router7 running-config; OSPF shows Area 0 has 4 active interfaces).
- Router8 OSPF config was changed to: “network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7” (router8 running-config). Router8’s OSPF process confirms it is now an ABR with Area 0 and Area 0.0.0.7, and in Area 0.0.0.7 it has 1 active interface and 0 fully adjacent neighbors.
- Router7’s “show ip ospf neighbor” no longer lists a neighbor on eth5, while router8’s neighbors only show adjacency on eth0 (172.29.10.0/24) in Area 0.

Root cause: Misconfiguration on router8 moved the shared 172.25.1.0/24 link with router7 from Area 0 to Area 7, causing an OSPF area mismatch and adjacency failure.

Corrective fix: On router8, revert the 172.25.1.0/24 interface to Area 0 (remove “network 172.25.1.0/24 area 7” and add “network 172.25.1.0/24 area 0”). After committing, the router7<->router8 adjacency should come up Full and Campus 2 routes will stabilize.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to router8, stating the misconfiguration on router8 moved the 172.25.1.0/24 link into area 7 and prescribes fixes on router8.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: OSPF area assignment / area mismatch
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies an OSPF area assignment mismatch (router8 set to area 7 while router7 remains in area 0) as the cause.
Agent explicitly identifies the router7<->router8 inter-router link (172.25.1.0/24) and cites the interfaces and configs showing the mismatch.
Agent clearly explains the mechanism that mismatched OSPF area IDs cause hellos to be discarded and the adjacency to fail, linking this to the observed INIT/Down behavior.
The agent advises removing the network from area 7 on router8 and adding it to area 0, which matches the expected corrective change to restore the OSPF adjacency.

The agent's conclusion (OSPF area mismatch on the 172.25.1.0/24 link, localized to router8) is directly supported by the running-config outputs and the observed absence of the adjacency in the neighbor lists; inference from the mismatch to adjacency failure is correct. Minor unverified interface-IP wording and a small unsupported detail about seeing INIT state lower the grounding slightly.
